summary:
Project ASTRO-X is an interactive 3D educational simulator designed to introduce users to the fundamentals of space mission planning and spacecraft design. Users can explore different mission objectives, assemble spacecraft using various components, monitor mass, power, cost and scientific capabilities, select orbital paths and launch vehicles, and experience a simulated launch with unexpected events.

The project transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. By allowing users to experiment with different spacecraft configurations and mission choices, it demonstrates how engineering decisions can influence mission outcomes. ORBIT ARCHITECT aims to make space exploration and mission design more accessible, encourage interest in aerospace engineering, and inspire users to understand the challenges behind real-world space missions.
details:
ASTRO-X is an interactive, browser-based 3D space mission design simulator that introduces users to the fundamentals of spacecraft engineering and mission planning. It allows users to experience the process of planning a space mission through a series of interactive stages.

Users begin by selecting a mission objective, such as Earth observation, deep-space communication, lunar orbit or a Mars flyby. They then assemble a spacecraft using different components, including solar panels, batteries, onboard computers and scientific instruments. The simulator provides mission diagnostics to help users consider important factors such as spacecraft mass, power requirements, budget and scientific capabilities. Users subsequently select an orbit and a suitable launch vehicle before entering a simulated launch sequence. During the simulation, unexpected events and anomalies require users to make decisions. A final mission report evaluates the outcome and provides a score.

The main benefit of ASTRO-X is that it makes complex aerospace engineering concepts more accessible through interactive experimentation rather than passive learning. It encourages users to understand how engineering decisions, resource limitations and mission requirements influence mission planning.

The project aims to promote interest in space exploration, aerospace engineering and STEM education, especially among students and beginners. Its creative approach combines a 3D space environment, spacecraft customization, interactive decision-making and mission evaluation into one educational experience.

The simulator was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D graphics, Tailwind CSS for interface styling and the Web Audio API for sound effects. Google Fonts is used for typography. The project was designed with usability, visual engagement, interactive learning and the balance between mission objectives and limited resources in mind.

ASTRO-X is an educational simulation, not an operational spacecraft control system or a substitute for professional mission-planning software.
